evidence.title: Noncritical takeover times vary with secondary task and individual response
evidence.observation: Source-reported finding: In self-paced noncritical simulator transitions, median automated-to-manual response was 4.567 seconds without a secondary task and 6.061 seconds while reading. Ranges were 1.975–25.750 and 3.179–20.994 seconds respectively. Post-transition steering variability did not significantly differ. Observation period and measurement context: Counterbalanced simulator sessions; calendar dates not established; 26 drivers.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded account; study or measurement; not independently reproduced
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative or qualifying; does not validate a definition

source_locations.SRC-141: Author-uploaded full article: Method, Table 2, Results, Discussion

evidence.limitations: Small simulator sample, noncritical prompts without a deadline and brief exposure. Response time is not stabilized safe control or hazard avoidance. Does not measure contemporary AI-agent supervision deadlines or faster feedback loops.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to other populations, tasks and operating environments remains unestablished. Missing measurement details are not inferred.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: Available intervention time and response variability require context; one universal response-time assumption is unwarranted.
evidence.dispute_status: See source version and dispute qualifications; no systematic clearance claimed.
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

terms.name: Chaperoning
terms.definition: The continuing supervisory activity of independently observing consequential behavior, exercising informed judgment, and intervening effectively when appropriate. This requires access, competence, authority, and an actual ability to alter outcomes—not nominal participation or an agent merely stating that an action is inappropriate.

relationships.explanation: Illustrates conditional response latency and variability, not a universal safe intervention window.
